title: Compass and Orchard
premise: In the border city of Vellamare, 1847, Mara Montrose inherits her dead master's unfinished atlas — and the hidden marginalia proving the crown's famine maps were falsified to justify seizing the valley orchards. When census taker Elias Thorne stumbles onto the evidence during a routine survey, the two are drawn into a race to publish the truth before the victors' historians burn the archives. Betrayed by the guild that trained her, Mara must choose between the atlas's perfection and the people it was meant to serve. In the end, she smuggles the corrected maps out with Elias's help, at the cost of her apprenticeship, her city, and nearly each other — but the record stands.
about_author: Isandro Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed cartography in Central European collections. Compass and Orchard is a debut novel born from a single annotated map found sewn into a ledger's spine.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Finishing her master Aldous's atlas in his cold workshop, Mara is interrupted by census taker Elias Thorne, whose questions about the valley's pre-famine population unsettle her — and who glimpses the falsified survey plates. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion, as the safe distance of 'history happening elsewhere' collapses into her own doorway.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elias returns at night, confessing his superiors ordered him to log the valley as 'uninhabited wasteland.' Together they decode Aldous's marginal notes proving the orchards were thriving when the crown starved them. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance kindling into trust — and the first tremor of love — as two careful people choose dangerous truth.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Guild Hall
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, climax. The Cartographers' Guild, exposed and pressured by the crown, declares Aldous a fraud and burns the master plates; Mara barely rescues the corrected valley sheets while Elias is arrested as an accomplice. Emotional beat: terror and fury at the peak — the price of survival demanded upfront, and Mara paying it with her name, her craft, and the man she loves.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, resolution. Freed by a sympathetic clerk, Elias files the census amendment with the corrected maps attached, forcing even the victors' historians to acknowledge the record. Mara departs for the coast with the atlas, Elias choosing exile beside her. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph — history was not something that happened to other people; they made it, and lost almost everything but the truth.
